chunks: My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. They said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us from Musa ibn al-Hasan and al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Ja'far ibn 'Uthman, from Sama'a ibn Mihran, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the Maghrib prayer: Sometimes we pray while we fear that the sun may still be behind the mountain, or that the mountain has concealed it from us. So he said: You are not required to climb the mountain.

key_terms.المغرب: Maghrib prayer - the sunset prayer, one of the five daily obligatory prayers in Islam
key_terms.صعود الجبل: Climbing the mountain - here meaning the unnecessary action of ascending to verify sunset

ai.seo_question: Do you need to verify sunset before praying Maghrib near mountains?
ai.summary: Sama'a ibn Mihran asked Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about the validity of Maghrib prayer when praying near mountains where the sun might be hidden behind a peak rather than truly set. The Imam eased their concern, ruling that one is not required to climb the mountain to verify sunset. This practical ruling reflects the principle of ease in Islamic jurisprudence and was addressed to the early Shia community where mountainous terrain made sunset verification difficult.

en.bilal-muhammad: My father and Muhammad b. al-Hasan (rh) narrated to us. They said: Sa`d b. `Abdullah narrated to us from Musa b. al-Hasan and al-Hasan b. `Ali from Ahmad b. Hilal from Muhammad b. Abi `Umayr from Ja`far b. `Uthman from Sama`a b. Mehran. He said:

I said to Abi `Abdillah (as) regarding Maghrib: We prayed, but we fear that the Sun was behind the mountain, and that the mountain had hid it from us. So, he said: You do not need to climb the mountain.
